tables.label: human-performance-on-pets
tables.caption: Comparison of human performance on Oxford IIT Pets. As in , the metric is average per-class classification accuracy. Most of the gain in performance when going from the human zero shot case to the human one shot case is on images that participants were highly uncertain on. "Guesses" refers to restricting the dataset to where participants selected an answer other than "I don't know", the "majority vote" is taking the most frequent (exclusive of ties) answer per image.

tables.label: dataset_ablation_table
tables.caption: CLIP performs similarly when trained on only YFCC100M. Comparing a ResNet-50 trained on only YFCC100M with a same sized subset of WIT shows similar average performance and number of wins on zero shot and linear classifier evals. However, large differences in dataset specific performance occur. We include performance on the 3 datasets where YFCC does best and worst compared to WIT according to a linear probe in order to highlight this as well as aggregate performance across all linear and zero-shot evals and the canonical ImageNet dataset.
